adjustedProfit.title: Net income vs adjusted profit
adjustedProfit.content:
Adjusted profit is management's non-IFRS measure: reported net income with one-off, non-cash items removed -- principally fair-value movements on the preferred shares that converted to ordinary shares on listing.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): FY2025 net income grew 108.6% YoY to RMB3,109.1m, but that includes a RMB556.9m non-cash fair-value gain on preferred shares booked around the Hong Kong listing (FY2024 carried a smaller RMB25.7m fair-value loss on the same line, so the YoY comparison is flattered on both sides). Adjusted profit strips this out and grew 66.9% to RMB2,574.8m -- still strong, but the headline growth rate overstates the underlying improvement by roughly 42 points.

What to watch:

  • The gap between net income growth and adjusted profit growth in any year with a preferred-share or other one-off fair-value swing
  • Management guides on adjusted profit margin, not statutory net margin -- use this line when comparing to their own targets
  • The preferred shares fully converted at listing, so this specific swing should not recur

storeNetwork.title: Store count and GMV
storeNetwork.content:
Store count is the number of franchise outlets in the Guming network; GMV (gross merchandise value) is the retail value of all drinks sold through those stores, upstream of the franchise fees and supply-chain revenue the company actually books.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): this is a franchisor, not a chain operator -- revenue is a cut of GMV via franchise fees plus equipment/ingredient supply, so store count and GMV growth are the leading indicators and reported Revenue is the lagging one.

What to watch:

  • GMV per store (GMV / store count) -- rising store count with flat per-store GMV signals saturation, not growth
  • Net new stores versus gross openings (closures hidden in a rising net count)

cupsSold.title: Cups sold
cupsSold.content:
Cups sold is the total number of drinks sold across the franchise network in the period -- the physical unit-volume behind GMV and revenue.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): cups sold grew from 1,328m (FY2024) to 1,905m (FY2025), +43.4% -- faster than the store count growth, implying higher throughput per store, not just network expansion. Only disclosed at FY year-end so far, not at the half-year mark.

What to watch:

  • Cups sold growth versus store count growth -- same-store volume is the harder, more durable growth source
  • Average selling price per cup (GMV / cups sold) for price/mix effects

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Guming Holdings Limited (古茗控股有限公司): the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
